criteria.quote: Lickitung licks filth clean, then makes it stink.
criteria.revision: Make the contradiction more explicitly source-grounded: "Lickitung’s Pokédex says it licks filth clean—but whatever it licks always stinks afterward."

criteria.quote: Its tongue can lick filth clean, according to its Pokédex.
criteria.revision: Add a concrete Lickitung detail without changing the angle: "Its over-six-foot tongue can lick filth clean, according to its Pokédex."

criteria.quote: If Lickitung removes the filth, why does the result still stink?
criteria.revision: Frame the unresolved issue as a contradiction rather than implying the research explains the cause: "If the filth is gone but the smell remains, does Lickitung’s Pokédex really get to call that clean?"

criteria.quote: That creates two outcomes: clean-looking, but still foul-smelling afterward.
criteria.revision: Replace this restatement with the documented consequence that failing to clean off its saliva causes an intense, persistent itch: "And if you don’t clean off a spot where it licked you, the Pokédex says an intense itch will set in—and won’t go away."

criteria.quote: But whatever Lickitung licks will always stink afterward, too.
criteria.revision: Delay the stink reveal until after establishing its cleaning ability: first present "It licks filth clean," then reveal, "But whatever it licks always stinks afterward." This lets the documented contradiction change the viewer’s impression of Lickitung instead of giving away both sides immediately.

criteria.quote: The filth is cleaned, but the Pokédex calls cleanliness questionable.
criteria.revision: Replace repeated cleanliness summaries with distinct evidence: use the over-six-foot tongue, its sticky saliva, and the Pokédex warning about an intense itch before returning to the stink contradiction.

criteria.quote: Lickitung may remove the grime, but its own Pokédex leaves the word clean debatable.
criteria.revision: Make the ending land on the source’s strongest wording: "Lickitung may lick the filth clean, but its own Pokédex admits whether it’s really clean is... questionable."

criteria.quote: Would you call that clean, or just less dirty?
